Stunning Nature magazine

Cover and a two-page spread for a magazine about rare natural phenomena. A rich cover in a split-complementary palette. There is a strong play on associations: green for nature, purple for lightning. The pages are easy to read and look clean and modern, but not boring.

FILE 04

Travelio landing page

Hero section for a travel agency. A minimal layout and warm colors that bring to mind travel, holidays and the sea, with a classic serif and sans-serif type pairing.

WebLanding page

FILE 05

Halloween party poster

A clean-looking poster with a clear hierarchy and a classic pair of complementary colors: orange and purple. The title uses a typical Halloween display font that sets the right playful tone, and it is paired with a font of the opposite mood: a restrained, organized, even slightly office-like sans serif. It makes all the necessary information easy to read and get across to the viewer. Still, I wanted something in between a fully professional and a casual poster, so I added a third, playful handwritten font for the line “Welcome to the party”. It works as a bridge, reminding you that this is a celebration and a party.

My design journey started with running social media for streamers (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube) and editing videos. The part I enjoyed most was the visuals: thumbnails that had to stand out, catch the viewer's eye and make them click on the video. Learning to design that kind of thing was really challenging for me, but also interesting.

Now I design more than just thumbnails: posters, editorial layouts, book covers and logos. I prefer a minimalist style with a cool color palette and plenty of space, but I really like to experiment and try something new, sometimes even the complete opposite of my usual style.

Games have been a big part of my life since childhood and shaped a lot of who I am, and becoming a professional Dota 2 player was a dream come true. I left esports, but games still inspire me in their own way, and this portfolio is the proof. Can you guess which game inspired it?

I pay close attention to details, but I don't like overloading a design with them. I learn fast and I'm open to new ideas. I have my own taste, but I try not to lock myself into it, so I keep studying very different styles to broaden my visual library. And esports taught me how to work in a team, because in a team game that matters more than anything.
